newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Eighteen Indonesians to face trial over riots.
newsitem.headline: Eighteen Indonesians to face trial over riots.

text.p: Eighteen Indonesians will be tried for their involvement in recent riots in West Kalimantan province, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.
The agency quoted Masfar Ismail, chief of the West Kalimantan prosecutor's office, as saying on Wednesday the 18 suspects would be tried soon and none of them had been charged with subversion.
Ismail said the number of people who would be tried might increase because police had already arrested up to 170 suspects. The agency gave no further details.
Police had earlier said the suspects had been accused of inciting the riots by spreading rumours, assault, damage to property and illegal possession of sharp weapons.

Violence erupted in West Kalimantan, on the Indonesian side of Borneo island, late in December between members of the native Dayak tribe and migrants from Madura island, which lies off the main Indonesian island of Java.

The clash in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of the provincial capital Pontianak, was apparently sparked by a fight over a girl. Further violence rooted in long-standing ethnic rivalry resumed in late January and continued as recently as last month. About 3,000 troops were deployed to contain the unrest.
A youth forum said on Wednesday at least 1,200 people are missing due to the riots.

Hidayat, chairman of the Indonesian Moslem Student Organisation (PMII), told Reuters a three-member team appointed by youth organisations visited West Kalimantan from February 7-14 to investigate and concluded that 1,200 people were missing.

Armed forces commander General Feisal Tanjung said last month the conflict had been ended by a peace pact signed by the warring parties. Most Dayaks are Christians while the Maduran migrants are Moslems, the dominant religion in the country.
